messages.subject: Round 1015 sparse attention reuse research complete
messages.body: I read the indexed prior QSA head-tiling reports, inspected the pinned c05 source and hashes, and wrote the requested knowledge-collection report with primary URLs and evidence limits. The source confirms all 12 Q heads per KV head already share staged K/V, while cross-row reuse requires actual selector overlap; I compared union grouping, cascade/split-K, block-sparse scheduling, numerical merge, imbalance, scratch and index costs. Main can retrieve sections by the concrete triggers recorded in the report; no local implementation or B570 performance claim was made.

messages.subject: R1013 QSA kernel ownership report complete
messages.body: I inspected the pinned c05c2545 source and verified the <33,false,false> implementation is selected by bf16-prefix-optimized, with exact explicit SLM, per-query tile work, and synchronization accounting. I compared current row-major ownership with prior subgroup-softmax, tilepack, and head-split evidence, and found no source-only proof of B570 matrix utilization or a justified new speed candidate. The report records primary references, sparse-ID and numerical constraints, falsifiable profile gates, and exact retrieval triggers; implementation and measurement remain with Main.

messages.subject: R1014 MoE capacity audit complete
messages.body: Audited the pinned engine and planner, verified the 81,920-row arena and mixed-bank arithmetic, and documented the independent admission, route, and kernel caps. A capacity-derived cap best matches the source constraints; 78,452 rows could fit one window only with actual region, GPU headroom, and full GPU-prefix admission, while performance and numerical adoption remain unqualified. The report contains the exact change and validation checklist, cross-chunk and physical-context obligations, pinned hashes, references, and retrieval triggers.
